newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Hortense bears down on Puerto Rico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Hortense bears down on Puerto Rico.

text.p: Tropical Storm Hortense threatens to unleash flash floods and landslides on Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands but has failed to whip up hurricane strength, the National Hurricane Centre said on Sunday.
The hurricane warning for the U.S. and British Virgin islands and Puerto Rico was discontinued as Hortense was not strengthening, the centre said.
Tropical storm warnings were still in effect and the centre said island residents should prepare for a direct hit.
Hortense posed a serious threat of landslides, mudslides and flash floods across the Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico, it said. Rainfall was expected to reach 5 to 10 inches (12-25 cm).
Forecasters said tropical storm strength winds were expected to hit St. Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands at about midnight local time (0400 GMT) on Sunday.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) on Sunday, the storm was located near latitude 16.3 north and longitude 63.4 west, about 125 miles (200 km) southeast of St. Croix.

Hortense's maximum sustained winds were 55 mph (89 kph), down from 60 mph (95 kph), and little change in strength was expected in the next 24 hours. It was moving west in line to Haiti and the Dominican Republic at nine mph (14 kph).

A hurricane or tropical storm warning indicates that hurricane or tropical storm conditions are expected within 24 hours. Hurricane and tropical storm watches are posted 36 hours ahead of possible landfall.
Hortense initially gathered strength in the wake of Hurricane Fran, which hit the U.S. coast on Thursday, wreaking havoc through the Carolinas and Virginia and killing at least 22 people.

The string of tiny Leeward Islands -- including Martinique, Dominica, Guadeloupe, Antigua, Montserrat, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the British Virgin Islands -- immediately issued tropical storm warnings and urged residents to prepare.
